official_sources: Enforcement notice appeals procedural guide England

official_measurement_examples.name: Current enforcement guidance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Enforcement and post-permission guidance was updated 6 May 2026; a breach of planning control and a formal enforcement notice remain distinct states.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal procedure date split
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Inspectorate maintains separate procedural guides for applications dated on or after 1 April 2026 and applications dated on or before 31 March 2026; the two routes must not be silently merged.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current appeal update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The post-1-April-2026 planning appeal guide was updated 16 July 2026 and the enforcement appeal guide 22 April 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission versus discharge
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission subject to conditions does not prove that later approval or discharge requirements have been satisfied.

official_measurement_examples.name: Pre-commencement condition
official_measurement_examples.fact: A valid pre-commencement condition can prevent lawful commencement until its requirement is met; permission alone is not evidence of lawful start.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 73 versioning
official_measurement_examples.fact: A section 73 decision creates a distinct permission route while the original permission can continue to exist; condition sets and decision dates must retain version context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Enforcement discretion
official_measurement_examples.fact: Issuing an enforcement notice is discretionary and requires the authority to consider breach and expediency; an allegation is not a served notice.

official_measurement_examples.name: Appeal ground distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: An enforcement appeal can rely on statutory grounds including ground (a), which is treated as a deemed planning application; this does not erase the enforcement case or automatically grant permission.

core_rules: planning permission is not condition discharge
pre-commencement condition compliance is distinct from permission grant
section73 permission and original permission retain separate version context
alleged breach is not a served enforcement notice
enforcement notice is distinct from breach-of-condition notice
enforcement action is discretionary and case-specific
appeal route must retain application-date regime
ground-a deemed application is not automatic permission
appeal submission is not appeal success
historic enforcement records retain effective and appeal dates
planning condition evidence is not ownership evidence
enforcement status does not calculate parcel development yield
expired or superseded notices must retain temporal status
no parcel enforcement clearance may be inferred from absence in one dataset
no Future Growth promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. May-July 2026 enforcement/appeal updates were preserved with permission, condition, breach, notice and appeal-stage separation; no parcel promotion.
